newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam institute sees currency sliding in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam institute sees currency sliding in Q2.

text.p: A rush to buy dollars in the second quarter of this year is likely to steepen the decline of the Vietnam dong, according to an official at the government's Market Research Institute.
The official was quoted by Wednesday's English-language Vietnam News as forecasting an exchange rate of around 11,600-11,800 dong to the dollar by the end of June.
The current level is around 11,185 dong to the dollar, and most analysts have been expecting a gradual fall to around 11,500 by the end of this year.
"...a run on the dollar is expected in the second quarter of this year because of the need to make massive purchases of the currency to pay for LCs (Letters of Credit)," Vietnam News said.

Bankers in Hanoi said they expected some fluctuations in the dong/dollar exchange rate between April and June, but the overall rate of depreciation was likely to remain stable at around one percent per quarter this year.
The central State Bank of Vietnam has followed a policy in recent months of allowing a gradual decline in the value of the dong.
Financial analysts say the measure is aimed chiefly at tackling a yawning trade deficit by making imports more expensive and exports cheaper. In 1996 the trade gap reached $4 billion.

Bankers in Ho Chi Minh City said the dong was trading at around 11,182 to the dollar on Wednesday, close to the lower limit of an official exchange fluctuation band for the currency of plus or minus one percent.
The State Bank's pivot rate was put at 11,077.
